Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Summary assessment from transcript aligned with DDx:
  - Acute asthma exacerbation (dust-triggered) suspected given history of childhood asthma, dust exposure, nocturnal worsening, wheeze with shortness of breath; plan includes objective testing and consideration of steroids.
  - Allergic bronchospasm / dust allergy likely contributing, given dust exposure and hay fever history; may overlap with asthma.
  - Acute bronchitis/viral bronchitis possible but less certain based on provided symptoms.
- Any contradictions or unsupported suggestions: None identified relative to transcript; DDx supports the transcript’s direction.

Management Plan
- Arrange in-person clinic evaluation to assess for asthma/allergy.
- Investigations: Pulse oximetry to assess oxygenation (SpO2) at clinic.
- Medications/therapies discussed: Consider antihistamine for potential dust allergy; steroids may be considered if asthma exacerbation confirmed after evaluation.
- Patient instructions: If antihistamine not available at home, can obtain OTC; GP may prescribe if needed.
- Communications: Write a letter to the patient’s GP detailing the visit; GP appointment expected to be brief.
- Follow-up: In-person GP visit for further assessment and documentation of current status and treatment plan.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Acute asthma exacerbation (dust-triggered) — High: Strongly supported by history of childhood asthma, dust exposure, nocturnal symptoms, wheeze with dyspnea.
- Allergic bronchospasm / dust allergy overlapping with asthma — Moderate-High: Dust exposure and hay fever history support allergic component contributing to bronchospasm.
- Acute bronchitis / viral bronchitis — Medium: Onset over 2 days with wheeze possible but less consistent due to absence of fever or productive cough described.
- Note: Vocal cord dysfunction and other airway causes considered lower likelihood given history favoring airway hyperreactivity; no conflicting evidence identified in transcript vs. DDx.
